text:
For a **pellet smoker**, I’d choose a **1,000Wh-or-larger power station** for an overnight cook. The auger and fan typically draw just 35–60W once running, but the igniter needs a brief higher-power surge; a typical 12-hour cook may use roughly 450–750Wh. Check your smoker’s startup wattage and the station’s surge rating before buying. ([Dealectric’s sizing guide](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

- **Best compact overnight pick: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2.** It has 1,070Wh and 1,500W output—enough capacity for a typical single overnight cook, with some headroom. ([Specs and comparison](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))
- **More reserve for campsite devices or multiple cooks: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2.** Its 2,073.6Wh capacity and 2,600W inverter provide more breathing room if you’ll also charge phones or run lights. ([Details and buy link](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

If you have a **small smoker and a shorter cook**, the 288Wh BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 is listed at about five hours for a 35W smoker—but it’s not the pick for an overnight run. ([Runtime estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

These recommendations are for **pellet grills**, not electric smokers with heating elements; those draw much more power and need a substantially larger station.
